rounds.proof_sketch: Input shape is [128, 1], so size=128. With block_size=256, num_blocks=1. Thread idx = threadIdx.x ranges 0-255. For idx >= 128, thread_loss=0.0f. Thread 255 writes 0.0f to shared_mem[255] (out-of-bounds in mutant with array size 255). During reduction at stride=128, thread 127 reads shared_mem[255]. Since thread 255 always writes 0.0f (because idx=255 >= size=128), the out-of-bounds location consistently holds 0.0f, making the mutation behaviorally equivalent for this fixed input size.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes shared_mem from size 256 to 255, causing thread 255 (threadIdx.x=255) to access out-of-bounds memory. However, with the fixed input shape [128, 1], thread 255 always computes thread_loss=0.0f because its global index (255) exceeds the data size (128). The out-of-bounds write of 0.0f happens to be benign - during reduction, when thread 127 reads shared_mem[255], it receives 0.0f (either from coincidental memory state or hardware tolerance of the small overflow). No input values can change what thread 255 writes, since it's always outside the valid data range. The mutation would only become observable with size >= 256, where thread 255 would have valid data producing non-zero loss.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The mutation causes undefined behavior (out-of-bounds access), but the accessed location is always written with 0.0f because thread 255 never processes valid input data (size=128 < thread_index=255). Killing requires input size >= 256, which requires a shape/configuration change not permitted by the contract.
rounds.recommendations: When testing shared memory sizing mutations, the test framework should include input sizes that utilize the full block size. For a block_size of 256, testing with at least size=256 would make all threads process valid data, exposing shared memory sizing errors. Additionally, tools like cuda-memcheck or compute-sanitizer should be integrated to detect out-of-bounds shared memory accesses regardless of whether they manifest as output differences.
